messages:
harper_infra: Planning a low-impact maintenance for eu-central racks next Thu 01:30-03:30 UTC. Purpose: staggered NIC microcode update + soft GPU driver reload to address packet drops we've seen at high QPS.

maintenance-bot: Maintenance ticket created: m-euc1-2026-04-02. Notifying subscribers.

nijel_sre: How are we sequencing? Last time parallel reannouncements pushed traffic spikes.

harper_infra: Sequence = single-rack windows, 7min cadence, pre-seed KV/prefix cache on target pool, and egress shaping for 12m per rack. We'll mark racks with label `maint_window=april2` to avoid accidental scheduling.

zoe_ops: Pre-seed script exists? I can run a pre-warm job to populate KV for common prompts to avoid cold-token penalties.
harper_infra: Yes — use ops/warmup/kv_seed.sh with `--shards 4`. Run 30m before each rack start.

priya_prod: Can we avoid impacting realtime inference tenants? Suggest moving them to redwood-dedicated-1 for the period. I can gate by tag `tier:realtime`.
harper_infra: Agreed. We'll create a migration plan and run a 20-tenant canary first. Priya, can you coordinate?

cory_fin: Cost note: spilling to dedicated/reserved is cheaper per-hour but scaling up capacity quickly may trigger on-demand accelerator procurement; estimate +0.4% daily infra spend if we migrate 200 instances for 2 hours. Approve?

zoe_ops: We can prefer warm standby (reserved) for realtime; only use on-demand burst for GPU-heavy batch jobs.

nijel_sre: Runbook bullet points:
- cordon rack nodes with `kubectl label node/$NODE maintenance=true`
- drain with 120s grace: `kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120`
- trigger NIC microcode update (kick BMC soft-reset if needed)
- unload GPU driver, reboot if driver doesn't detach cleanly
- after node ready -> run kv/prefix cache validation job -> uncordon

harper_infra: Inline check commands for on-call:
```
kubectl label node/$NODE maintenance=true
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
ssh $NODE sudo /opt/firmware/update_nic.sh --apply
# if nic flaps >2 then ssh $BMC sudo bmcsoftreset
ssh $NODE sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia || true
ssh $NODE sudo reboot
kubectl uncordon $NODE
```

priya_prod: I'll publish the tenant list to the shared sheet and start canary migrations tonight at 22:00 UTC.

nijel_sre: Alerts/abort criteria: pause/abort if any of:
- p95 text-gen latency increases >120ms over baseline
- error rate +4% sustained for 10m
- egress queue depth >80% for 3 checks
If triggered, we'll pause the run and shift pending racks to eu-west-2 warm pool.

cory_fin: I'll set a spend burn alert at +0.75% and an ops tax approval threshold at +1.5%. Finance will be paged if we cross +1.5%.

maintenance-bot: Reminder set: Thu 01:30 UTC  m-euc1-2026-04-02. Channel: #eng-infra.

harper_infra: Prechecks: telemetry probes in place?

nijel_sre: Yes — synthetic probes for gen latency + kv hit-rate. Added dashboard: Gen p95, KV hit-rate, Egress queue. Also added a short post-rack smoke: run `ops/test/smoke_gen.sh --size 256` after each uncordon.

zoe_ops: Can we tag hardware-replacement candidates automatically? If a node has >3 NIC dips during the window, add tag `hw_replace_candidate=true` and open hw ticket.
harper_infra: Good idea. I'll add a small script to the runbook to append those to ops/hw_replace.csv.

priya_prod: Canary tonight results: 10 canary tenants show no latency regression. I'll report in the thread after run.

cory_fin: All set on alerts.

harper_infra: Final owners: Nijel (on-call), Zoe (ops runbooks & warmup), Priya (tenant migration), Cory (spend). I'll run comms and the window. Postmortem template will be auto-created by maintenance-bot after completion.

maintenance-bot: m-euc1-2026-04-02 status: scheduled.
